subject: Computer Networking
title: Service Workers
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Service Workers.

hook.text: What if your web app worked offline? Service workers intercept network requests and serve cached responses.

buildup.text: A service worker is JavaScript that runs in the background, separate from the page. It acts as a proxy.

discovery.text: On install, it pre-caches critical files. On fetch, it serves from cache first, then updates from the network.

twist.text: Service workers power push notifications and background sync too. They make web apps feel native.

climax.text: PWAs — Progressive Web Apps — use service workers to install on your home screen and work offline.

punchline.text: Service workers make the web work offline. Apps without the app store.

quiz.question: What role does a service worker play in a web app?
options: It intercepts network requests and can serve cached responses
It compiles JavaScript into native code
It manages the browser's tab layout

details.summary: Service workers are JavaScript scripts that run in the background between the browser and network, intercepting requests, caching resources, and enabling offline functionality.
details.whyItMatters: Service workers transform websites into app-like experiences that work offline, load instantly on repeat visits, and receive push notifications. They bridge the gap between web and native applications.
takeaways: Service workers intercept network requests as a programmable proxy
Cached resources enable offline functionality and instant loads
Push notifications and background sync work without an open tab

faq.question: How do service workers enable offline functionality?
faq.answer: Service workers intercept every network request from the page. A caching strategy determines whether to serve from cache, network, or a combination. The cache-first strategy serves cached resources instantly and updates them in the background. This makes previously visited pages available offline.

faq.question: What is a progressive web app?
faq.answer: A PWA is a website that uses service workers, a manifest file, and responsive design to deliver an app-like experience. PWAs can be installed on the home screen, work offline, send push notifications, and load instantly. They use web technologies but feel like native applications.
